title: The discography compiled by a French doctor
summary: Dr. Kochlin of Paris gave him a discography running from 1926 to the sixties, with first recording in 1926 with Luis Russell and sessions with Jelly Roll Morton and Johnny Dodds, and tunes he had forgotten.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I was looking at the discography that
you have here that was compiled by a doctor friend of yours in France?
Yeah.
What's his name?
Oh, I don't know. What's his name, Dr. Foulibout? [q.v. below]
Oh, well, we'll get his name in a minute.
Anyway, the discography goes from 1926 all the way up into the sixties. And that was your first recording in 1926 with Luis Russell?
Right.
And you recorded with a lot of very interesting people. I think in 1926 also with Jelly Roll Morton.
Right.
And Johnny Dodds.
Right.
Dr. Kochlin, K-o-c-h-l-i-n. Kochlin.
Kochlin, Dr. Kochlin.
It's French, (unintelligible) in Paris.
He's French.
Is he someone you met when you've been playing in France?
No, he met me. I didn't meet him,
because I didn't even know him. In fact, he brought that and I thought he had forgotten it on the desk, but he said, "No, I brought that for you." I said, "Oh, thank you."

So I was looking at that and I said gosh, there's a lot of things in there I didn't even know -- tunes that I had written years ago -- myself, that's the only time I heard when I looked at this -- these things he gave me here.
